sections.heading: SEO and AI search in Garden Grove
sections.body_html:
Garden Grove, in northern Orange County, had 171,949 residents at the 2020 census, making it the county's fifth most populous city. State Route 22, the Garden Grove Freeway, runs east to west through it, and the western part of the city is known as West Garden Grove.

Wikipedia notes that Korean Americans began moving to Garden Grove in the 1970s, creating the area known as Little Seoul or Koreatown. The city is also home to Christ Cathedral, and its Strawberry Festival over Memorial Day weekend, started in 1958, is estimated to draw 250,000 visitors.

sections.heading: How Garden Grove customers search
sections.body_html:
That mix makes Garden Grove searches unusually multilingual. Residents search for restaurants, salons, clinics, insurance and home services in English, Korean, Vietnamese and Spanish, often on phones and often by naming the neighborhood.

Visitors arriving for the festival or for Koreatown's restaurants search for food, parking and things to do nearby, and they increasingly ask AI assistants for a single recommendation.

sections.heading: How Google ranks local results in Garden Grove
sections.body_html:
Google is unusually direct about local rankings. Its Business Profile help says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and popularity. It describes prominence as how well-known a business is, based partly on how many websites link to it and how many reviews it has, and says more reviews and positive ratings can help. The same page adds that there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking.

Garden Grove sits between Anaheim, Santa Ana and Westminster, so local results overlap with neighboring cities. A precise address, an accurate service area and reviews that mention Garden Grove help Google connect you to searches here.

sections.heading: Getting recommended by ChatGPT and Google AI in Garden Grove
sections.body_html:
AI assistants answer Garden Grove questions best when a business describes itself clearly, in the languages its customers use, with consistent details across its profile, website and directories.

Ask these questions in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google each month and record who is named:

  1. What is the best Korean barbecue in Garden Grove?
  2. Which insurance agent in Garden Grove speaks Korean?
  3. Who is a good plumber in West Garden Grove?
  4. Which dentist in Garden Grove has evening hours?
  5. Where should I eat near the Strawberry Festival?

sections.body_html: Real local mentions in Garden Grove come from community and cultural organizations, business associations, festival sponsorships and local media in the languages your customers read. Earned mentions help; bought links can break Google's spam policies.

sections.heading: Business Profile basics
sections.body_html:
Your Google Business Profile is usually the first thing people see in a local search.

Google's guidelines say service-area businesses, which serve customers at their locations, should have one profile for the central office or location with a designated service area. A rented mailing address you do not operate from, a virtual office, is not eligible, and P.O. boxes are not acceptable. Your business name should be your real-world name as used on your storefront, website and stationery, without extra keywords.

sections.heading: Reviews
sections.body_html:
Ask every customer for a review, in whichever language they prefer. Reviews that mention the service and the neighborhood help both Google and AI assistants.

Google's Maps content policy prohibits fake engagement: reviews must reflect a genuine experience, and businesses may not offer incentives, such as payment, discounts or free services, in exchange for a review or for removing a negative one. Ask every real customer, make it easy with a direct link, and reply to reviews.

sections.heading: Structured data
sections.body_html: Add LocalBusiness structured data, or the most specific Schema.org type for your business, with your real name, address, phone, hours and service area, matching your Business Profile exactly. Google's local business documentation explains how this markup can help it show your details.

sections.heading: City pages that help Garden Grove customers
sections.body_html:
If you serve Koreatown or West Garden Grove specifically, describe the real work you do there; a page that only swaps the city name helps no one.

Google's spam policies list pages targeted at specific cities that funnel visitors to one page, and substantially similar pages, as doorway abuse. Create a city page only when you have something specific to say about work there, such as local projects, permits or response times, and link it clearly from your main service pages.
